source_terms:
Imagery as a Source
what happens if the visual aspects of imagery are allowed to rule, so to speak—to determine not only the compositional structure of a project overall, but the compositional and stylistic attributes of the type?
Typography is always a pattern of lines, but images present a radically greater range of form languages
item.claim: Bringing type and image together is described as notoriously difficult because each has formal characteristics most often at odds with the other, and because the two are usually assumed to be mutually dominant and referential. The source proposes inverting that assumption and letting the imagery rule — determining not only the project's overall compositional structure but the compositional and stylistic attributes of the type. Its reason is that typography is always a pattern of lines whereas images present a radically greater range of form languages, so applying an image's language to text quickly relieves a designer of presumptions about how text should behave and how layouts ought to be organised. Two directions are named: one in which typographic elements become in essence part of the imagery, and one in which the imagery sets up the logic for how type responds to it pictorially while the type retains its identity as a separate entity alongside the images.

mechanism.text: Type's form language is narrow — lines — so it cannot supply the variety a layout needs; imagery can, and letting it lead breaks the designer's default assumptions about text behaviour rather than arguing with them.

scope.conditions: projects that carry substantial image material

caveats.text: The source is explicit that the correspondence need not be literal: in one study the sizes, positions and radii of type arcs are not direct repetitions of any attribute in the image, and the mere fact of them is enough to create the visual connection. That weakens the method into a judgement call with no test.
Every instance is a layout this lane could not see. The two named directions are recorded because they are stated in words; the visual result of either is not inferred.

source_stated_problems: type and image are notoriously challenging to bring together; each has its own formal characteristics most often at odds with the other
source_stated_remedies: let the imagery determine the compositional structure and the type's compositional and stylistic attributes
either absorb the typographic elements into the imagery, or let the imagery set the logic to which separate type responds

positive.description: an exhibition poster whose titling and text typography are composed and styled to become one with a field of forensic bone images, with transparency, overlapped edges and misaligned grids inside the imagery informing font choices and forcing text into cut-out areas that look grid-based but are not
a promotional calendar in which each month's date matrix changes in width, depth and weekday-list orientation in response to the formal conditions of that month's photograph
running text set flush right so that the difference between its aligned edge and its irregular rag echoes the hard, soft, dark and light stems of a bamboo image

intra_source_relations.note: one of the alternative systems context may select
the inverse operation — bending the image toward the environment rather than the environment toward the image

provenance.section: Alternative Architectures — Intuitive, Relational, and Conceptual: 'Imagery as a Source' (spine 6)

source_terms: pay attention to contrast in the medium
the tonal range should be contrasting enough to allow the mark or symbol to be clearly identified
item.claim: The source names two contrast relationships that must both hold when the mark is applied to promotional material or corporate stationery: the contrast between the logo and its background, and the contrast between the actual elements inside the logo. It sets one pass condition covering both — the tonal range must be contrasting enough for the mark or symbol to be clearly identified.

scope.conditions: applying an existing mark to stationery and promotional material, i.e. at the application stage rather than the design stage

caveats.text: no numeric threshold, no measurement method, and no definition of 'clearly identified'. This source supplies the two relationships to check, not a criterion for passing them.
the internal-contrast half is the less obvious of the two and is the one a designer working only against white will not have tested

source_stated_problems: a mark that cannot be clearly identified against its background or within itself
source_stated_remedies: keep an eye on both contrast relationships when applying the mark

intra_source_relations.note: reversal is the case in which the ground contrast changes

provenance.section: tip 16 'Pay attention to contrast in the medium' (printed 187)

item.source_title: Google, "ABCDs of effective video ads" — Google Ads Help, Google for Business resources and Think with Google (retrieved 30 August 2026)
item.source_locator: Google for Business resources, "ABCDs of effective video ads", footnote to the headline statistics; Google Ads Help, section "Benefits", asterisked source note; Think with Google, "Sources (1)"
item.question: What study are the 30% and 17% figures attributed to, and which of the three pages tells you the sample size?
item.answer: All three attribute them to a Google/Kantar study called "The Short & the Long of ABCDs Effectiveness", global, dated April 2021 — but only the Google for Business resources article gives a sample, "n=11,000 ads". Google Ads Help cites the same study, publisher, scope and month with no sample size. Think with Google cites it as "Google/Kantar Link AI, Global, The Short and the Long of ABCDs Effectiveness, 2021", naming Kantar's Link AI, dropping the month and giving no sample size. The study itself is not linked or published on any of the pages.
item.support: The three footnotes differ as described. n=11,000 ads appears only in the resources article's footnote.
confounders: attributing the sample size to the Google Ads Help page, which is the page most often cited but does not give it
assuming n=11,000 refers to people surveyed rather than ads
conflating this Kantar study with the separate Ipsos collaboration described on Think with Google, which has no stated sample

item.source_title: David Airey, Logo Design Love: A Guide to Creating Iconic Brand Identities (New Riders, 2010)
item.question: Airey does not treat simplicity as one requirement among seven equals. What does he say it does, and what are the three specific consequences he works through?
item.answer: He states that a simple logo helps satisfy most of the other requirements of iconic design — so on his own account simplicity is the member of the set that buys the others, not a peer of them. The three consequences he works through in order are: versatility, because a minimalist approach lets the mark be used across a wide range of media, from posters down to a website favicon; recognisability, which he says raises the chance of achieving a timeless, lasting quality; and memorability, because it is much easier to remember a single detail than five. He extends the dependency elsewhere — the small-size requirement is met only by simplifying, and the distinctiveness route he recommends works by removing colour so that shape carries the mark.
item.support: Printed p. 22 states the enabling claim and the versatility consequence; p. 23 gives recognisability and memorability; p. 34 makes the small-size dependency explicit.
confounders: listing the seven elements as unstructured peers, which loses the one piece of structure he supplies
attributing to him a mechanism for WHY recognisability produces longevity — he asserts the link without arguing it
confusing versatility with adaptability across cultures; his versatility claim is about media and carriers

source_terms: in projects boasting a significant amount of text, arguably the type is the most important component
Basing a grid’s attributes on those of the text’s typography ought to be considered one of the first practical strategies to pursue when building a grid.
item.claim: Layout approaches vary in how far they emphasise images or text, but where a project carries a significant amount of text the type is arguably the most important component: the more text there is, the harder it is to assimilate and the more work it demands of the viewer. Basing the grid's attributes on the attributes of the text's typography should therefore be one of the first practical strategies pursued.

mechanism.text: Reading difficulty scales with text volume, so in a text-heavy project the measure that most affects the reader is the one the structure should be built from.

scope.conditions: projects with a significant amount of running text

caveats.text: "arguably" is the source's own hedge and is the only one it places on this ordering of importance

intra_source_relations.note: one of the strategies for building a grid
the column-width derivation that follows from it
the image-proportion strategy starts from the other component

provenance.section: Building a Grid — Based on Textsetting Attributes: Designing to Read

source_terms: the simplest solution is usually the most effective
a simple logo helps satisfy most of the other requirements of iconic design
item.claim: Simplicity is not one attribute among equals in this source: it is the one that buys the others. The source states the reason directly — a simple mark helps satisfy most of the remaining requirements — and then spends three sub-sections demonstrating the three channels: simplicity makes a mark more versatile across media, easier to recognise (hence more likely to endure), and easier to remember.

mechanism.text: A simple mark carries fewer elements, so it survives reduction, reproduces in more media, is recognised faster, and leaves less for a viewer to hold in memory. The source gives all three consequences explicitly and treats them as one causal chain running from simplicity.

scope.conditions: marks intended for wide application across media and long service

caveats.text: the source nowhere defines 'simple' operationally; the nearest thing to a test it offers is the one-inch reduction (sk_logo_0006) and the describability test (sk_logo_0014)
'usually the most effective' is a hedge the source itself supplies

source_stated_problems: a mark carrying more detail than the smallest application can hold
